scene: A cartoon man with swept-back grey hair, a beige round face, solid black eye sockets and a wide grin of sharp white teeth stands with both black hands raised and fingers curled, wearing a black suit and red tie. A jagged red line falls from the upper left across the frame, dips behind him and keeps descending toward the lower right. The backdrop is a black-to-grey spotlight glow.
mechanism: The single printed surname plus a grinning cartoon figure over a collapsing red line turns the title's anonymous 'one man' into a named villain with a loss story.
composition: MADOFF spans the top third in one row and the grinning head sits at centre just below it, so the eye drops straight down from word to face. The red line works as a diagonal that crosses behind the shoulders and gives the lower half a second, quieter focal path.
typography: One white block-capital word fills roughly two-thirds of the width with strong contrast against the black top of the frame and stays crisp at 160x90. It supplies a name the title never gives, while the $65 Billion figure and the word scam appear only in the title.
colors: Near-black background with a pale grey glow behind the head, a beige face, a black suit and two saturated red accents (the falling line and the tie). The red is the only chroma on the frame and reads as loss.
psychology: Black eye sockets, a wide toothy grin and clawed raised hands give the figure a menacing, gleeful look rather than a trustworthy one. The falling red line adds a loss cue, and no victim or human reaction is shown.
partnership: The title withholds the name and states the amount, the thumbnail supplies the name and the collapse and leaves the amount to the title. Together they answer who and how much, with the method of the scam left open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white MADOFF word first, then the toothy grin, then the red line sliding down the left and right sides.
art: Flat cartoon with thick dark outlines and a soft radial gradient; the head and hands are clean cutouts on the dark ground. The native file is only 360x202, so the line work is slightly soft, but the shapes survive reduction.
strength: A named subject and a falling red line give a complete villain-plus-collapse proposition with one word of text.
weakness: Nothing on the frame conveys scale or method, so the $65 Billion hook lives only in the title.
bottleneck: The grin is a cartoon villain stereotype, which makes the image easy to read but leaves no detail that separates this story from other fraud-explainer frames.
action: Hypothesis: test adding a short '$65B' tag beside the falling line to see whether putting the number on the image strengthens the specificity.
counterexample: Seq 19 adds a crowd, a podium and a gold bag so the story is a scene, where this frame relies on one face and a line.
expression_label: wide toothy grin with black eye sockets
hero_object: grinning man over falling red line
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Two stick figures face each other across a gap on a rocky ridge at sunset. The left one has shaggy brown hair and a fur tunic, with lowered brows, wide eyes glancing to the side and a flat mouth. The right one is a plain white-headed stick figure with a torn brown scrap on one shoulder, small raised brows and a neutral mouth. A low sun sits behind the left figure; a boulder occupies the gap between the figures.
mechanism: A two-figure standoff at dusk turns the extinction question into a confrontation: one hairy, one smooth, with the headline asking who ended whom.
composition: The headline occupies the top band; two figures stand on opposite sides of the ridge. The low sun sits behind the left figure, while a boulder separates the figures near the center.
typography: Three words in thick yellow capitals with a black outline run edge to edge across the top and stay fully readable at 160x90. They are a clipped version of the title and add only the plural 'others', so the subject human species is carried by the pictures.
colors: An orange-to-yellow sunset sky dominates, with brown rocks and tunics below and one hot yellow headline. The saturated warm field makes the white stick heads pop as the brightest shapes in the middle band.
psychology: The fur-clad figure's lowered brows and sideways glare contrast with the other figure's blank stare, which reads as a wary face-off. The dusk lighting adds a sense of an ending, but no weapon or violence is drawn.
partnership: The thumbnail shortens the title's question to its verb and pairs it with a two-species picture, so it repeats the premise and adds a visual casting of who the 'others' are. Whether the answer is yes is left open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline, then shaggy left figure, plain right figure and the low sun behind the left figure.
art: Doodle-style cartoon with wobbly outlines, a gradient sky and layered rock shapes, and no mismatched shadows visible. The heads are only about a sixth of the frame height, so the brow detail shrinks to dots at 160x90.
strength: Contrast between a hairy figure and a bare stick figure makes the two-species premise legible without any caption.
weakness: The facial expressions are small and the figures are thin, so the emotional beat is faint compared with the headline.
bottleneck: Headline and figures sit in separate bands, so the question mark and the confrontation do not interact.
action: Hypothesis: crop in so both heads fill the middle half of the frame to test whether larger faces lift the confrontation.
counterexample: Seq 3 puts enormous faces with extreme expressions in the foreground, where this frame keeps small, quiet heads.
expression_label: side-eyed frown versus neutral stare
hero_object: shaggy caveman figure facing a stick figure
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Three cartoon bust portraits sit in a row below one huge word. At left, a blond man with a long braid and beard has a red streak down one blue eye and screams with an open mouth. At centre, a figure in a dark green steel helmet presses both hands over nose and mouth with eyes rolled upward. At right, a pale woman with long platinum hair, dark blue lips, blue eyes and gold cross earrings looks sideways at the viewer.
mechanism: Three exaggerated historical archetypes under one country name sell the 'entire history' title as a cast of contrasting characters.
composition: The word fills the top 40 percent edge to edge and the three busts are packed into the bottom 60 percent with the helmeted figure at centre, slightly higher than the flanking two. White outlines isolate each cutout and the symmetric trio holds the eye on the centre face.
typography: One 7-letter word in heavy black condensed capitals spans the whole width, readable at any size, and sits in contrast with white background. It names the subject only; the entire history and explained parts of the title are not on the image.
colors: Pure white ground with black lettering and three tonal groups: gold-yellow hair at left, olive helmet and skin pinks at centre, and pale silver hair with black clothing at right. Blue irises and the red face streak are the small saturated accents.
psychology: One figure screams with a wide-open mouth, the central one hides the lower face and rolls the eyes up, and the third gives a cool sideways stare. The mix reads as rage, exasperation and detachment, which signals a comic tone rather than a serious one.
partnership: The country name restates the title's subject, and the three faces hint at eras or types without saying which. They turn 'entire history' into a question of who these people are.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: GERMANY first, then the central helmeted face and hands, then the screaming left face, then the pale right face.
art: Detailed digital illustration with consistent line weight, hatching on skin and clean white cutout borders, and the hands and facial features are anatomically coherent. Each bust is a separate cutout, so the lighting differs slightly between them, but nothing looks malformed.
strength: A giant one-word headline over three high-expression faces gives instantly legible topic plus character variety.
weakness: The three characters are not labelled, so the viewer cannot tell what period or events they stand for.
bottleneck: The centre figure's covered face hides the strongest emotion cue, leaving the screamer at left to carry the expression.
action: Hypothesis: add a small era marker (a year range on each bust) to test whether sorting the trio into periods sharpens the 'entire history' promise.
counterexample: Seq 20 uses the same giant-headline-over-faces layout for MEXICO, with a denser row of caricatures that lacks this frame's centre anchor.
expression_label: scream, hands over face with eyes rolled up, sideways stare
hero_object: helmeted figure with hands over face
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: WHERE DID IT ALL GO WRONG? / THE "PRINTING WIKIPEDIA" PART. / [BZZT BZZT] / [what if?]
scene: Two blank-headed stick figures stand among stacks of black-lined paper. The left one is hunched on top of the tallest stacks with one hand at its chin and three small motion ticks beside its head. The right one stands upright at the edge of a lower pile. A small printer sits between them with the sound words BZZT BZZT above it, and a red circle in the bottom left corner holds a black dinosaur silhouette hanging from ropes beside the white words what if?
mechanism: A two-line joke dialogue next to towering paper stacks makes the title's absurd premise visible as a punchline, but the writing is small.
composition: The left figure on the paper tower and the printer form a loose triangle, and the right figure stands apart on a mostly empty white field. The red corner circle anchors the lower left and is the single colour block, while the two speech lines sit in the upper area with no clear lead.
typography: Twelve words in thin hand-lettered capitals sit in two speech lines at the top plus the white what if? wordmark on red. At 160x90 the speech lines shrink to hairlines and only the red wordmark and the paper stacks stay recognisable. The text restates 'printing Wikipedia' from the title and adds the where-did-it-go-wrong joke.
colors: Black line art on a pure white ground, with a single flat red circle in the lower-left corner as the only colour. The white-and-black contrast is high but the red patch is a brand mark rather than a message signal.
psychology: The left figure's chin-on-hand pose and motion ticks suggest exhaustion or regret, while the right figure's plain stance is neutral. The humour comes from the dialogue, not from facial expression, since neither head has facial features.
partnership: The title poses a hypothetical about printing Wikipedia and the image answers with a deadpan quip, so the two work as a setup and a joke. It does not reveal what happens when you print it.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the paper stacks and seated figure first, then the red what if? circle, then the speech lines, with the printer and BZZT last.
art: Clean xkcd-style marker linework with hand-drawn letters and no gradients or shading, a deliberate flat look. Several paper-stack lines are densely repeated, but the line weight is even and the background is empty.
strength: A recognisable minimal comic panel with a joke visible in the dialogue gives a strong, unmistakable channel identity.
weakness: The speech lines are thin and small, and the stick heads have no facial features to carry emotion.
bottleneck: At phone size the dialogue becomes illegible, so the joke that carries the thumbnail disappears.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge only the right-hand line, "THE PRINTING WIKIPEDIA PART", to roughly double its height to test whether a single readable line holds at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 2 puts a single thick headline over a coloured sky, making the premise legible at 160x90 where this frame does not.
expression_label: NONE
hero_object: paper stacks with printer and seated stick figure
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A full-width red banner holds the headline above a blue gradient field. At left, a white ceramic bowl of amber liquid with whole dried cloves floating in it. At right, two glossy liver renders: the upper one is orange-brown with dark pitted spots, the lower one is smooth maroon. Two curved yellow arrows run from the spotted liver down to the smooth one.
mechanism: A spotted liver arrowed into a smooth healthy one beside a bowl of clove tea suggests the drink fixes the organ, with a demand to stop ignoring it.
composition: The banner caps the frame, the bowl fills the left half and the livers stack in the right half, so the layout reads left-to-right as cause, then effect. The two yellow arrows loop from the top liver to the bottom one and carry the eye down the right column.
typography: Four words in heavy sans-serif capitals, white for STOP IGNORING and yellow for CLOVE TEA, sit on solid red and are legible at 160x90. The text names only the drink and the command; the 7-day, 10-effects and body parts of the title are carried by the livers.
colors: A red banner, a cool blue background, amber tea and orange-brown tissue, with bright yellow arrows and headline words. The red-and-yellow header uses alarm colours while the blue field makes the warm bowl and liver pop.
psychology: No person appears; the alarm comes from the imperative STOP, the red banner and the contrast between a pitted and a smooth organ. The implied claim is a body repair, which presses on health anxiety.
partnership: The title promises unspecified effects after 7 days and the image picks one: a damaged liver turning healthy. This narrows the title's open list to a single dramatic outcome.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red banner first, then the spotted liver, down the yellow arrows to the smooth liver, then the bowl of cloves.
art: Photographic bowl and cloves beside two smooth 3D-rendered livers, giving a mixed realism with sharp specular highlights. The spotted liver is a stylised render with dark pits, so the diseased-versus-healthy contrast is exaggerated, and there is no human subject to inspect for artefacts.
strength: The bowl-to-before/after-organ layout reads at a glance and the red banner makes the command impossible to miss.
weakness: The damaged-to-healthy liver pair is an unqualified transformation claim with no timeframe or condition stated on the image.
bottleneck: The sensational organ transformation is the dominant message, so it outweighs the title's neutral list of effects.
action: Hypothesis: replace the spotted-to-smooth liver pair with a neutral labelled body-system icon row to test whether clicks hold without the implied reversal.
counterexample: Seq 10 also arrows a food to a person but shows a human face, where this frame shows only organs and food.
expression_label: NONE
hero_object: bowl of cloves and spotted-to-smooth liver pair
medical_notes: The pitted-to-smooth liver pair with arrows implies clove tea repairs a diseased organ, which the title does not claim and the image does not support.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: DASH diet to lower blood pressure / Dietary Approach to Stopping Hypertension (DASH) / High intake of vegetables, fruits, low-fat dairy / AND THE DIET INVOLVED A HIGH INTAKE OF VEGETABLES, FRUITS, AND LOW-FAT DAIRY. / [Leslie Kernisan, MD MPH] / [BetterHealthWhileAging.net]
scene: A vertical video frame sits in the middle of a blurred teal pillarbox. Inside it, a teal title bar carries bold text, below it is a white slide with one bulleted line, a rounded teal caption box with all-caps text overlaps the lower edge of the slide, and a woman with dark curly hair looks at the camera with a closed mouth in front of a pale wall with a small shelf. A microphone tip shows at the bottom and a teal footer holds a web address.
mechanism: A talking-head lecture frame with the diagnosis-style slide text states the topic plainly and relies on a named physician's caption for authority.
composition: The frame is a narrow centre column about a third of the width, with blurred teal side fields doing nothing. Within it four text blocks stack above the small face, so the face is the lowest and smallest element.
typography: Dense wording spans a title bar, slide heading, bullet, repeated all-caps caption, name/credential label and website. At 160x90 the narrow central strip makes this text unreadable.
colors: Muted teal throughout, with a white slide panel and black text, and no accent colour. The monochrome teal blurred sides and teal bars leave every block at similar visual weight.
psychology: The presenter's level gaze, closed mouth and plain background read as calm and clinical. The credential in the name label carries the trust cue; no urgency, fear or surprise is shown.
partnership: The title states how DASH lowers blood pressure; the slide adds vegetables, fruits and low-fat dairy plus a printed credential. The caption repeats the bullet, but those details extend the adjacent title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the dark bold header at the top of the column first, then the caption box, then the woman's face, with the footer last.
art: Screen-grab of a vertical video with a blurred background extension, standard slide fonts and a natural, evenly lit webcam face. There is no stylisation and no composited element; the only artefact is the stretched blurred sidebands.
strength: The named MD MPH label and the slide-style text make the frame look like a genuine clinical explainer.
weakness: Four text blocks plus a small face leave no single focal point, and the whole thing is unreadable at phone size.
bottleneck: The usable area is only the central third of the thumbnail, so the strongest cue, the credential, is too small to read.
action: Hypothesis: replace the frame with a crop of the presenter's face plus the words DASH DIET at 80px height to test whether one readable phrase outperforms the slide grab.
mechanism_secondary: clinician named on a slide frame
counterexample: Seq 12 shows a doctor-style presenter too, but with a large headline and a highlighted shoulder, where this frame leaves the speaker small and the text dense.
expression_label: neutral level gaze, closed mouth
hero_object: slide text with presenter webcam
medical_notes: The frame states a standard diet description with a visible clinician credential and makes no cure or reversal claim.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A stick figure with a round white head, one raised brow, eyes glancing to the right and a hand on its chin stands between two grey plates by a lake. On the left plate a smiling cartoon cow with brown and white patches lies above a glossy red steak with sparkle marks. On the right plate a green crocodile with an open smile lies above a dull grey-brown steak with two flies and small vapour lines, and two more flies hover over the water.
mechanism: Putting a sparkling steak next to a dull, fly-bothered one makes the title's 'never eat' question a visual choice between beef and crocodile.
composition: The stick figure sits at the exact centre and splits the frame into two matching plates, the cow on the left and the crocodile on the right, under a full-width yellow headline. The mirrored layout makes the thinking figure the hinge between two options.
typography: Two words and a question mark in thick yellow capitals with a heavy black outline span the full top and remain fully readable at 160x90. The text repeats the title's key noun and drops the word 'never', which the plate contrast supplies.
colors: Yellow headline over a blue sky, olive lake, brown cow and green crocodile, with a bright red steak as the hottest accent on the left. The red-versus-grey steak colour gap is the main value signal in the lower half.
psychology: The figure's raised brow, sideways glance and chin-on-hand pose read as hesitation. The sparkling steak versus the fly-surrounded steak signals appeal versus disgust without any gore.
partnership: The title asks why humans avoid crocodile meat, and the image supplies a ready visual answer in the form of an unappetising steak and flies. It leaves the actual reason open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow headline first, then the thinking stick figure, then the crocodile on the right, then the cow and its red steak.
art: Glossy cartoon style with thick outlines and consistent colouring, a plain stick figure placed in a detailed lake scene. The stick figure is flat and outlined while the animals are shaded, so the mix of styles is visible, but nothing is distorted.
strength: The cow-versus-crocodile pairing with a hesitating figure in the middle frames a clear either-or question.
weakness: The background lake, cattails, plates and flies add detail around the three subjects without adding information.
bottleneck: The two steaks are small in the bottom corners, so the key good-versus-bad contrast is the weakest part at phone size.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the two steaks and remove the background reeds to test whether the red versus grey comparison carries the premise.
counterexample: Seq 11 uses one stick figure and one headline too, but in a single-subject scene with a clock, where this frame stages two options.
expression_label: raised brow, side glance, hand on chin
hero_object: crocodile and cow on plates with steaks
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: At left, a smiling cartoon man with dark purple hair, a pink polo, beige trousers and white sneakers strides forward carrying a glass jar of gold coins. A cream-coloured path winds up a green mountain, lined with stacks of green banknote bundles with tan bands. The summit holds a pile of coins and cash behind a glowing yellow sunburst and the word MILLIONAIRE in white-gold block letters.
mechanism: A man with a jar of coins walking a winding path up a cash-lined peak pictures the journey from a small saving habit to the word MILLIONAIRE.
composition: The black headline sits top left, the walker bottom left, and the path curves from his feet to the glowing summit at the upper right, forming an S that leads the eye across the frame. The sunburst makes the summit the brightest point and the walker the nearest, so the story reads as before and after in space.
typography: HOW I DID IT is in huge black block capitals and MILLIONAIRE is in a smaller outlined white-and-gold 3D style on the summit; both are legible at 160x90 though the second is much smaller. Together they give a first-person claim the title does not state, while the average salary part is not shown.
colors: White background with green hills and bills, cream path, a yellow sunburst at the top and black headline text. The pink shirt gives the walker a distinct local colour against the green.
psychology: The walker's wide eyes, closed smile and steady stride read as upbeat and confident. The glowing summit supplies aspiration, and no strain or setback is shown along the path.
partnership: The title offers a how-to for an average earner, while the image tells a first-person success story with the end state labelled. The path suggests a long steady climb rather than a trick.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: HOW I DID IT first, then the walking man with the coin jar, then the winding path up to the glowing MILLIONAIRE summit.
art: Polished cartoon illustration with soft shading, clean outlines and a bright radial glow, and the cash stacks, path and figure are all coherent. The man is outlined as a clean cutout against white, and the scene has no obvious artefacts.
strength: One continuous path from a coin jar to a glowing summit tells the whole transformation in a single readable image.
weakness: The first-person phrase and the generic cartoon man carry no evidence of who did it or from what salary.
bottleneck: MILLIONAIRE is much smaller than the headline and sits against a busy sunburst, so the payoff word is the second thing to be read.
action: Hypothesis: add a small salary figure beside the jar to test whether a concrete starting number makes the average-salary promise credible.
counterexample: Seq 15 shows the finance-success idea with a single large number and a safe, where this frame shows a pictured journey.
expression_label: wide-eyed closed smile
hero_object: man carrying coin jar up cash-lined path
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A semi-realistic illustrated man with a buzzed fade haircut and trimmed beard glares forward with lowered brows and a closed mouth. Tattoos cover his neck, a robed-figure portrait sits in an oval on his bare chest, and a gold chain with a cross hangs over it. He wears an open black shirt and holds a gold-coloured rifle with a folding stock across the lower left. A thin black curved arrow above the text points up-left toward his head.
mechanism: A tattooed, armed figure beside the words No Way Out frames the cartoonised rank ladder as a one-way trap rather than a career.
composition: The man fills the left 60 percent at chest-up scale with the rifle cutting diagonally across the bottom left, and the text block sits at upper right on white. The rifle diagonal and the up-left arrow both point back at his face, so the layout funnels to the glare.
typography: Two lines of thin rounded handwriting-style type: a red No above a black Way Out, set in the right third with generous white around it. The words stay legible at 160x90 but are light in weight, and nothing on the image names the cartel or its ranks that the title promises.
colors: White background, black shirt, warm skin tones, a gold rifle and chain, and one red word. The gold of the rifle and chain is the only warm metal, giving the lower left a brighter edge than the text side.
psychology: Lowered brows, a set mouth and direct gaze are visible. The rifle supplies a threat cue; tattoos and jewelry describe the character design without independently proving criminal affiliation.
partnership: The title promises a rank-by-rank cartel walk-through, and the image shows one armed, tattooed man with a no-escape phrase. It supplies the criminal setting but not the ranks or the country.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the glaring face first, then the red No, then Way Out, then the gold rifle at the lower left.
art: Digital illustration with outlined shading, fine tattoo detail and a clean cutout on white. The hands are mostly out of frame and the rifle outline is coherent, so there are no visible anatomy artefacts.
strength: One hard stare plus a gold rifle gives an immediate danger-world cue on a clean white field.
weakness: The phrase No Way Out names no rank, number or place, so the image gives no sign that the video covers a ladder.
bottleneck: The same phrase and arrow layout appears on Seq 13, so the text reads as a channel template instead of this story.
action: Hypothesis: replace the red No with a numbered rank label (for example 'Rank 1') to test whether a ladder cue connects the image to the title's every-rank promise.
counterexample: Seq 13 repeats the same text and arrow with no weapon and a clean-cut face, showing the template with a quieter threat level.
expression_label: lowered brows, direct glare, flat mouth
hero_object: tattooed man with gold rifle
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: IMPORTANT FOR SENIORS / PEANUT BUTTER BEFORE BED
scene: An older woman with white-grey hair, freckled and wrinkled skin, lies on a blue patterned pillow in a pink floral gown under a blanket, looking at the viewer with a closed mouth. At right, a glass jar of peanut butter holds a silver spoon lifting a thick swirl. A bright red arrow starts under the first headline line and points down-right at the jar. The background is a dark navy glow.
mechanism: A bedridden-looking senior beside a jar with a red arrow turns the title's overnight claim into a single focus on peanut butter at bedtime.
composition: Headline bars sit at the top and bottom, the woman fills the left half and the jar fills the right half with its spoon reaching the top-right corner. The red arrow runs on a diagonal between her face and the jar, so the eye travels from person to food.
typography: Seven words over two bands: white block capitals at the top and a yellow PEANUT BUTTER with a white BEFORE BED at the bottom, all with thick edges and fully readable at 160x90. The bottom line states the item and timing, and the top line adds the audience, while the title's age 50 and overnight-effects hook are absent.
colors: A dark blue background carries white and yellow text, a saturated red arrow and warm orange-brown peanut butter. The warm jar and the red arrow are the only hot areas, which pulls the eye away from the pale face.
psychology: The woman rests against a pillow with level gaze and closed mouth. IMPORTANT and the red arrow add emphasis; the bedside setting may suggest vulnerability but does not establish illness or frailty.
partnership: The title asserts that after 50 the body needs peanut butter before bed and promises overnight effects; the thumbnail repeats the item and timing and adds the senior audience. It does not state what the effects are.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: IMPORTANT FOR SENIORS first, then the red arrow, then the peanut butter jar, then the woman's face and the bottom line.
art: Glossy photographic rendering with a polished jar and crisp spoon highlight, while the woman's skin has a slightly smooth look. The pillow, gown and blanket are consistent, and there are no visible mismatched shadows or malformed details.
strength: The arrow gives a clear person-to-food path, and the bottom line names the item and the timing in readable letters.
weakness: No benefit or outcome appears on the image, so the viewer is left with the instruction without a reason.
bottleneck: The frail bedside setting implies illness, which confuses whether the message is prevention or treatment.
action: Hypothesis: move the woman to a seated, upright pose at a kitchen table to test whether a non-hospital setting removes the illness implication.
counterexample: Seq 6 shows a calm, text-heavy lecture slide with no arrow, so it has none of the urgency this frame stacks up.
expression_label: drawn brows, level stare, closed mouth
hero_object: peanut butter jar with spoon
medical_notes: IMPORTANT FOR SENIORS and PEANUT BUTTER BEFORE BED provide a food instruction without identifying a benefit; title claims require content context.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A stick-figure old man with grey hair lies on a pillow in a hospital-style bed, wearing a light-blue gown, with wide round eyes turned upward, raised wrinkled brows and a small open mouth. Behind him hangs a large wall clock with both hands pointing near 12. On the right, a masked stick-figure doctor in a white coat with dark hair points at a monitor whose green trace drops into a flattening line.
mechanism: A clock at midnight and a flattening heart trace beside a wide-eyed patient turns 'final moments' into a ticking countdown.
composition: The yellow headline runs across the top, the patient's large head sits left of centre, the clock rises behind it, and the doctor and monitor stand at right. The clock sits between the two figures and ties the patient's face to the monitor line.
typography: Three words in thick yellow capitals with a black outline fill the top edge; the numeral 60 is the same size as the letters and all of it remains readable at 160x90. The text turns the title's vague final moments into a specific 60-second window.
colors: A pale grey-blue hospital room gives a muted base, with one yellow headline, a light-blue gown, a green monitor trace and the black outlines. The green trace is the only chroma on the right and the yellow on top is the loudest element.
psychology: The patient's upturned wide eyes, lifted brows and slightly open mouth read as dread, while the masked doctor pointing at the line is calm. The clock and flattened trace stack time-running-out cues.
partnership: The title asks what happens before death and the image narrows it to a minute with a clock and monitor as the stage. It poses the sequence without revealing it.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: FINAL 60 SECONDS? first, then the patient's wide-eyed face, then the clock, then the monitor trace and the doctor's pointing hand.
art: Flat doodle-style stick-figure drawing with a bold outline and minimal shading, consistent across the bed, clock and monitor. The clock numerals are legible at native size and the layout is clean, with a plain wall as background.
strength: Face, clock and flat-lining monitor all point at the same moment, so the premise needs no explanation.
weakness: The medical details are small and the doctor's face is covered, so the emotional load rests on the single patient face.
bottleneck: The clock nearly covers the patient's shoulder and overlaps his head, which makes two of the focal elements compete for the same area.
action: Hypothesis: move the clock to the empty top-right of the wall to test whether separating it from the patient's head makes the face-plus-clock sequence cleaner.
counterexample: Seq 7 uses the same stick-figure house style and top headline for a lighter either-or question, where this frame stages a darker countdown.

scene: A bearded man with dark hair and thin-framed glasses stands in a navy polo shirt and crosses his forearms, resting one hand on the opposite shoulder and holding the other palm open beneath it, which has a red-orange glow on it. His brows are pulled together and his mouth is slightly open. Behind him, a pale semi-transparent second image of the same man stands with one arm stretched out in a living room. A small orange arrow at the left of his upper arm points up toward his head, and a blurred blue sofa fills the left background.
mechanism: A man gripping a glowing shoulder under the words AFTER 60 FROZEN SHOULDER? presents the title's symptom as a recognisable pose, with a faded stretching double hinting at the exercise answer.
composition: The text stack occupies the left 45 percent and the large head-and-shoulders figure fills the centre and right, with the red-and-white AFTER 60 tag above the headline. The red glow on the gripped shoulder sits at the right-centre of the frame and the ghosted figure behind him fills the upper right.
typography: Four words in three tiers: a white-on-red AFTER 60 tag, a huge white FROZEN and a yellow SHOULDER? with a question mark; all three tiers stay readable at 160x90. The text matches the title's first phrase and omits the five exercises and the mobility promise.
colors: A soft blurred pale-blue living room supports a navy shirt, white and yellow lettering, a red tag and a red-orange pain glow. The glow and tag are the only reds, which makes the shoulder and the age marker the sharpest points of colour.
psychology: Drawn-together brows, a slightly open mouth and a hand clamped on the shoulder read as discomfort aimed at the viewer. The ghosted outstretched-arm image adds a hint of relief or movement, and the red glow adds a pain cue.
partnership: The title offers a diagnosis question plus five gentle exercises, and the thumbnail shows the symptom and the age while hinting at movement with the ghost figure. It leaves the exercises themselves for the video.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white FROZEN word and the man's worried face first, then the red glow on the shoulder, then the AFTER 60 tag and the faded second figure.
art: Photographic portrait with sharp focus on the man and a deliberately blurred room. The ghosted second figure is a visibly transparent overlay with a pale halo, so the frame is a composite, and the red glow is a soft airbrushed effect rather than a physical feature.
strength: The gripped, glowing shoulder with a worried face identifies the condition and the audience age in one glance.
weakness: The faded second figure behind the main subject is small and washed-out, so the exercise hint barely registers.
bottleneck: The gaze and the red glow both pull toward pain, so the 'gentle exercises' half of the title has almost no visual presence.
action: Hypothesis: replace the faded double with a clear, saturated second panel of the same man mid-stretch to test whether a visible relief half raises the promise's clarity.
counterexample: Seq 21 shows a stitched chest scar with fatal-warning wording, whereas this frame uses an AFTER 60 age marker and a symptom question.
expression_label: drawn brows, slightly open mouth, hand on shoulder
hero_object: man gripping glowing shoulder
medical_notes: The thumbnail poses a symptom as a question with no cure or instant-relief claim, and the title promises gentle exercises.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A semi-realistic illustrated man with swept-back dark hair greying at the temples, stubble, lowered brows and a closed mouth stares straight ahead in a grey-green polo. mechanism: A stern, tattooed man in ordinary clothes next to No Way Out hints at an organised-crime world with no exit, without any weapon.
composition: The head and collar fill the left 55 percent, centred in its own column, and the text stack sits right of the face on a white field. The arrow bends back toward the hairline, so the right-hand words feed back into the face.
typography: Two lines of thin rounded type, a red No over a black Way Out, set in the right 40 percent of the frame with no competing text. Both lines read at 160x90, but the weight is light compared with the dark face, and nothing on the image says Albanian, mafia or rank.
colors: White background with a dark charcoal polo, warm tan skin, a muted tattoo and one red word. The dark clothing and hair block make the face the highest-contrast zone.
psychology: Furrowed brows, a fixed forward stare and a tight mouth read as stern and controlled. The neck tattoo is the only rough-edge cue and there is no weapon or aggressive gesture.
partnership: The title names a specific mafia and a rank-by-rank format; the thumbnail reuses a generic no-exit phrase and a tattooed figure that could belong to any criminal group. The nationality and the ranks remain unsaid.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the stern face first, then the red No, then Way Out, with the arrow looping back to the head.
art: Digital illustration with crisp contour shading and detailed skin texture, cut out cleanly on white. The neck tattoo is rendered with readable eagle and snake shapes and two small glyphs, and the collar and shoulders are coherent.
strength: A large, centred face with a direct stare is the unambiguous first read on a clean white background.
weakness: The text and the image carry no Albanian cue or rank cue, so the title's specificity is absent from the frame.
bottleneck: The light thin lettering is dwarfed by the dark face, so No Way Out reads as an afterthought rather than a hook.
action: Hypothesis: set the text in a heavy weight at about 1.5 times the current size to test whether a stronger caption balances the face.
counterexample: Seq 9 uses the identical text and arrow with a visible gold rifle and chest tattoos, showing a heavier threat cue than this unarmed frame.

hero_object: tattooed man's face and neck

text: RICH / RETIREES / OWN THESE [prop labels: SOLD, DIVIDEND PAPERS, BOND CERTIFICATES]
scene: A cartoon older man with swept-back grey hair, round glasses and a grey goatee glances to the side with one raised brow. He wears a blue blazer over a grey turtleneck, brown corduroy trousers, brown shoes and a wristwatch, and hugs a bundle: a small house with a SOLD sign, a sheaf labelled DIVIDEND PAPERS and a rolled scroll labelled BOND CERTIFICATES. A thick black curved arrow under the headline points down-left toward his lower legs.
mechanism: A well-dressed older man clutching a house, dividend papers and bonds under the words RICH RETIREES OWN THESE offers a literal armful of what the answer looks like.
composition: The figure stands in the left third at near full height and the headline stack fills the right 60 percent in three heavy lines, with the arrow curving between them. The bundle sits at chest height in the middle of the figure, so the props are at the same level as the first headline word.
typography: Four heavy black condensed words stack in three lines at the right, the middle line RETIREES widest, all with extreme contrast against white and fully readable at 160x90. The words nearly repeat the title's subject and the props add three asset types, but the prop labels shrink to specks at small size.
colors: White background, black headline, a blue blazer, brown trousers and a few yellow-tan paper tones. The restrained palette puts all the contrast in the black text and the figure's navy jacket.
psychology: A raised brow and a sideways glance, with arms wrapped around valuables, read as knowing and protective. The age cues of grey hair and beard make the audience clear, and nothing signals urgency.
partnership: The title promises seven boring assets, and the thumbnail shows a handful of three recognisable types without labelling them as boring. It turns the list into a picture but gives away part of the answer.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the big word RETIREES first, then the man's glance and his armful of props, then the arrow at the bottom.
art: Clean cartoon with a coherent outline weight, a distinct cutout on white and readable prop labels at native size. The arrow points at the man's legs rather than at the bundle, which makes its target a little ambiguous.
strength: Three labelled objects in one armful make the abstract title concrete with a single glance.
weakness: The arrow aims at his shoes instead of the props, so its role in the layout is unclear.
bottleneck: Only three of the seven assets in the title are pictured, so the specific list promise is weakly signalled.
action: Hypothesis: redraw the arrow to end at the bundle and test whether pointing at the assets makes the 'these' in the headline land.
counterexample: Seq 22 uses a similar headline-plus-arrow layout but points at a car rather than at a held bundle, giving a single wealth sign instead of a collection.
expression_label: raised brow, sideways glance
hero_object: armful of house, dividend papers and bond scroll
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with an egg-shaped bald-looking head and thin brown hair stands at left in a navy polo and jeans, eyes sliding to the right with a closed smirk. Next to him a red shopping bag carries a glowing red sports car on top, and a glowing green safe at the right shows stacks of green coins inside. A black curved arrow below WHO? points down-left at the safe.
mechanism: A red spending bag versus a green coin safe beside the giant figure $100K frames the first-100-thousand milestone as a choice and asks who makes it.
composition: The huge $100K fills the top right, WHO? sits beneath it, and the figure stands at the left edge with the bag and safe in the lower middle. The black arrow from WHO? curves down to the safe, linking the question to the green option.
typography: A four-character $100K in giant black block type and a smaller WHO? form a two-tier stack, both readable at 160x90 with maximum contrast. The text repeats the title's $100k figure and adds a question the title does not ask, while the 75 percent fail statistic is absent.
colors: Pure white ground, black headline, a red glow on the bag and car and a green glow on the safe. Red carries the spend side and green the save side, so the pair works as a value contrast.
psychology: The man's sideways glance and flat smirk read as sceptical, and his body points toward the objects rather than at the viewer. The red-versus-green glows frame one option as indulgent and the other as safe.
partnership: The title is about how hard the first $100k is and why 75 percent fail; the thumbnail adds a spend-versus-save picture and asks who succeeds. The reasons for failure remain open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: $100K first, then WHO?, then the arrow down to the green safe, then the red bag and the man.
art: Clean cartoon of the figure with a flat fill, while the car, bag and safe are glossy with a neon glow edge. The two rendering styles differ, but both are crisp on the white ground and there are no distorted shapes.
strength: The red-bag versus green-safe pair makes the save-or-spend choice readable with no extra words.
weakness: The figure's sideways glance is small and the smirk is mild, so the emotional cue is weaker than the headline.
bottleneck: WHO? is vague about whether it asks who fails, who saves or who reaches $100K, so the question has no clear target.
action: Hypothesis: change WHO? to a share such as '75%' beside the safe to test whether the title's own statistic makes the question land.
counterexample: Seq 16 uses the same cartoon-man house style but fills the frame with embedded clips and three text blocks, where this frame keeps two objects and one number.
expression_label: sideways glance, flat smirk
hero_object: $100K headline with red bag and green safe

text: DON'T DO THIS... / POOR / WTF???? / [broke but with all the apple stuff] / [I SPENT ALL MY SAVINGS ON THESE NFTs,] / [NFT on five cards]
scene: A cartoon man with a large pale head and thin brown hair stands at left with eyes shut, one hand pressed over his brow and his mouth open in a grimace, in a light-blue shirt. Two framed clips sit side by side at right. The left clip shows a woman in a denim jacket and jeans photographing herself in an arched mirror with a phone over her face, amid a pile of laptops and computers on a worn floor. The right clip shows a smiling man holding five cartoon NFT cards. A red POOR label tops the left clip and a green WTF???? label tops the right one.
mechanism: A facepalming cartoon beside two found-footage clips of dubious spending turns the long-form title into a pair of cringe examples.
composition: The cartoon head takes the left third at large scale, the DON'T DO THIS... headline spans the upper right, and the two portrait clips share the lower right. The two clips are the same size and side by side, so the eye has no ranking between them.
typography: Five main words across the headline and the two coloured labels, plus two caption lines inside the clips. The headline and the labels stay readable at 160x90, but the captions inside the clips shrink to illegible bars. The text adds the warning tone but not the 31 minutes of the title.
colors: White background, black headline, a red POOR label and a green WTF???? label, a light-blue shirt and muted greys and blues inside the clips. The red and green label colours sit on the same row, which makes them compete with each other.
psychology: Closed eyes, a hand over the brow and an open grimace read as exasperation, giving a clear reaction to the clips. The two real-person clips add social-proof-style evidence but carry little emotion at small size.
partnership: The title promises a 31-minute watch-along of money wasted; the thumbnail supplies two sample clips and a reaction. The title's length and its things-no-longer-worth-it angle are not shown.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the cartoon man's hand-on-brow face first, then DON'T DO THIS..., then POOR and WTF????, then the two clips.
art: A flat-coloured cartoon beside two photographic stills from social videos; the three sources have clearly different styles and framing, so the frame is a collage. The clips are cropped to portrait boxes with black borders, and the in-clip captions are small and soft.
strength: The facepalm reaction at large scale gives an instantly readable reaction cue next to the clips.
weakness: The two clips show small people and tiny captions, so the actual wasteful items are hard to make out at phone size.
bottleneck: Three text elements and two clips split attention across five zones, so no single item wins after the reaction face.
action: Hypothesis: keep only the NFT clip enlarged to the full right half and drop the other clip to test whether one clear example reads better than two small ones.
counterexample: Seq 15 holds a single number and two objects on white, which is much simpler than this frame's five-zone layout.
expression_label: eyes shut, hand over brow, grimace
hero_object: facepalming cartoon man beside two clips
